data.narrative:
Planted Solar, a Series A-stage climate and energy company founded by Eric Brown, has raised $32M to date. The valuation universe for frontier-energy ventures spans 1 public comparable (LNZA) and 8 private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable valuation approach. Using total raised ($32M) as a proxy for implied post-money valuation at Series A, a 2.0x step-up multiplier—typical for progression to the next funding stage—yields an implied valuation of $64M. This method reflects the company's position in the funding continuum and typical venture dilution patterns. Peer-median analysis could not be applied: while 8 Climate & Energy peers exist broadly, none met narrow filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables (fewer than 3 datapoints in each category). Substituting an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The triangulated range is $54M–$74M, with a median of $64M, anchored solely on stage-progression methodology. This range reflects ±15% variance bands around the point estimate. Key uncertainties include (1) the absence of granular peer data at identical stage and valuation tier, limiting cross-validation; (2) sensitivity to assumed step-up multiplier; and (3) market-specific conditions in frontier energy that may not track broader venture stage norms. Additional comparable transactions or revised assumptions on capital progression velocity could meaningfully shift this range.
